[Meeting header]
Date: 2025-09-19 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Ravi Patel (Redwood SE); Claire Thompson (Azimuth - Head of Cloud Security); Leo Marin (Azimuth - CTO); Jamal Ortiz (Azimuth - Compliance)

Summary:
Claire and team walked through Azimuth's regulatory and data residency constraints for customer data (banking). Main asks: SOC 2 evidence, ISO cert, SAML/SSO and RBAC mapping, audit log retention policy, and explicit confirmation that Redwood does not use customer prompts or content to train models unless customer opts in. Redwood confirmed default non-training policy, options for telemetry redaction, KMS/BYOK support on Dedicated/Private, and ability to provision EU-only tenant for pilot. Next steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 docs, schedule security questionnaire, spin up trial tenant.

Topics: SOC2, ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS/BYOK, data residency, prompt retention, PII/PHI, training policy.

- Maya to send SOC 2 and ISO docs

Transcript body:
[00:00:03] Maya (AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call before we jump in.
[00:00:08] Claire (Azimuth): Claire here.
[00:00:10] Leo (Azimuth): Leo on from the CTO side.
[00:00:12] Jamal (Azimuth): Jamal, compliance.
[00:00:14] Ravi (Redwood SE): Ravi, engineer.
[00:00:16] Maya: Great — goal today is to walk through Azimuth's security checklist, make sure we confirm 'no training' on customer data, and cover KMS/BYOK and residency options.
[00:00:30] Claire: Yeah, so I'll be blunt — for regulated banking data we need explicit commitments. SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001, SSO, RBAC mapping, audit logs with a 7-year retention for certain events, and confirmation that prompts won't be used to update models.
[00:00:46] Maya: Totally understood. We can start with the SOC 2 and ISO pieces — I'll share our latest reports after this call. For SSO we support SAML-based SSO and OIDC; RBAC is configurable in the console for roles and scopes.
[00:01:05] Leo: On SSO — can we map our internal groups to Redwood roles? And do you support SCIM for provisioning?
[00:01:12] Ravi: Yes, group-to-role mapping is possible, and we do support SCIM for provisioning users. There are some nuances on groups sync frequency but it's standard.
[00:01:25] Jamal: About audit logs — are the logs tamper-evident? Can we pull them out to our SIEM?
[00:01:31] Maya: Logs are exportable via the console or API; we can push to your S3 bucket or via syslog depending on the plan. We include request/response hashes, timestamps, client IPs, and model selection. Tamper-evidence is handled via signed logs in Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted customers get a standard audit trail.
[00:01:54] Claire: What's your retention by default for logs and for prompts/content?
[00:01:58] Ravi: Default for hosted is 30 days for request payloads and 90 days for aggregated telemetry; but we have options — Dedicated and Private give you full control. Also, we can set long-term retention for audit events.
[00:02:15] Claire: We need a 7-year retention for certain transactions. Is that feasible?
[00:02:19] Maya: Absolutely for Dedicated/Private. For hosted — we can discuss extended retention as an add-on; typically we replicate audit events to customer-owned storage for long-term retention.
[00:02:33] Leo: Encryption — in transit and at rest, yes? What KMS options exist? BYOK? HSM?
[00:02:39] Ravi: TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit. At rest we use cloud KMS by default. For Dedicated and Private, we support customer-managed keys (KMS) and HSM/B Y O K options depending on deployment and cloud provider. There's also an HSM-backed key wrap option for stricter controls.
[00:02:56] Jamal: We need FIPS-validated modules.
[00:02:59] Ravi: For BYOK we can integrate with your KMS that uses FIPS modules; for on-prem HSMs we support PKCS#11 integrations — we'll surface the compliance matrix in the docs I share.
[00:03:15] Claire: Ok — prompt content. This is core: will Redwood use Azimuth prompts or outputs to further train or fine-tune models?
[00:03:22] Maya: Short answer: No — Redwood does not use customer prompts or content to train models by default. We have an explicit opt-in program for any data used in model training, and that requires a contract addendum. We also provide configurable telemetry filters and redaction hooks.
[00:03:40] Claire: Can you put that in writing? Legal will want exact language.
[00:03:44] Maya: Yep, we'll include a clause in our standard DPA and the security pack I send. I'll include the exact phrasing: 'Redwood Inference will not use customer content, prompts, or outputs to train, improve, or fine-tune models without explicit, written customer consent.'
[00:04:00] Leo: Do you retain prompts for any debugging or quality monitoring?
[00:04:05] Ravi: We retain short-lived request traces for debugging — default 30 days — and aggregated anonymized metrics long term. For analysis we can anonymize or hash PII. If you need zero retention, Dedicated/Private can be configured to not store request payloads beyond transient memory; hosted customers can request disabled retention or route logs to customer storage.
[00:04:25] Jamal: PII / PHI handling — we treat prompt content as potentially sensitive. What are your redaction options?
[00:04:31] Ravi: We have pre-request redaction hooks you can run client-side, server-side redaction rules in the console, and post-request scrubbers. Also, we support policies to block storing tokens that match regex patterns, and integrate with data loss prevention (DLP) solutions.
[00:04:50] Claire: HIPAA isn't our primary need but some third parties will require PHI-level controls — do you have attestation?
[00:04:56] Maya: We can sign Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) for Private deployments; for hosted we'd need to discuss scope — usually larger enterprise customers opt for Dedicated or Private for HIPAA workloads.
[00:05:10] Leo: On telemetry — are you collecting model params, gradients, or anything that could be reverse-engineered?
[00:05:16] Ravi: No model internals. We collect service metrics, latency, error rates, usage counts, and anonymized token-level statistics for billing and performance. No gradients, no model weights.
[00:05:30] Claire: Great. About data residency — we prefer EU-only processing for EU customers. Can you provision tenant in eu-west-1 and ensure no cross-region replication?
[00:05:38] Maya: Yes, Dedicated and Private allow single-region deployments with no cross-region backups unless you opt in. For hosted we also have region pins — EU-only tenancy is possible for enterprise customers and pilot can be provisioned in eu-west-1.
[00:05:55] Jamal: For audit logs, we need a signed, immutable export monthly. Is that possible?
[00:06:00] Ravi: We can schedule monthly signed exports to your S3, with object signatures for tamper detection. That's a standard setup for our Dedicated customers.
[00:06:10] Claire: One more on 'no training' — if an engineer at Redwood accidentally looks at a prompt for debugging, is that covered?
[00:06:18] Maya: Access is role-based and audited; debug access goes through requestable access controls with justification and is logged. For sensitive environments we can configure a 'no human access' policy where only automated systems can access transient traces unless an emergency process is followed.
[00:06:35] Leo: Can you describe the emergency process?
[00:06:38] Ravi: It's a four-eyes approval: an engineer files a request, which must be approved by an on-call security lead, and the access is time-limited and fully logged; customer is notified per contractual terms if access involves customer content.
[00:06:55] Claire: Good. Also, we'd like to see proof of SOC 2 Type II covering 'change management' and 'access controls' specifically.
[00:07:02] Maya: We'll highlight those sections in the report we share.
[00:07:06] Jamal: For RBAC mapping — any limitations on number of roles or granular permissions? We need fine-grained control down to model and route level.
[00:07:15] Ravi: The console supports role scoping by model, route, and environment. There's no hard limit on number of roles; we can integrate with your IAM for role claims and translate them to Redwood roles via SCIM or SAML attributes.
[00:07:33] Leo: What about model version pinning and rollbacks — we need to ensure predictable behavior for production prompts.
[00:07:39] Ravi: You can pin model versions per route and we support canary rollouts, A/B routing, and automatic fallbacks. Rollbacks are immediate and logged.
[00:07:51] Claire: On billing and data retention — if we route logs to our S3, who pays for long-term S3 storage?
[00:07:56] Maya: Typically the customer covers their storage costs. We'll include recommended lifecycle policies in our guide to reduce cost (e.g., move old audit events to Glacier).
[00:08:10] Jamal: Are there any third-party subprocessors? We need a list.
[00:08:14] Maya: Yes — cloud providers we use (AWS/GCP), analytics providers for anonymized metrics, and our monitoring vendor. I'll include the subprocessor list and SOC attestations in the packet.
[00:08:27] Leo: Competitors we looked at include ApexAI and CloudModelCorp — we want to benchmark costs and controls.
[00:08:34] Maya: Totally — we can run a short perf/cost pilot and provide a comparison sheet.
[00:08:40] Claire: Ok, last logistics — can we get a 2-week pilot in EU region with KMS BYOK enabled and audit export to our S3?
[00:08:49] Ravi: Yes, we can provision that. I'll need an admin contact and your KMS endpoint details for BYOK.
[00:08:56] Jamal: I'll coordinate that with Ravi.
[00:09:00] Maya: Great, recap: Maya sends SOC2/ISO certs and subprocessors list; Ravi sets up EU pilot with BYOK and audit export; Claire/Jamal complete the security questionnaire. We'll sync next week to confirm tenant details.
[00:09:16] Leo: Sounds good.
[00:09:18] Claire: Thanks everyone.
[00:09:20] Maya: Thank you — we'll follow up via email with the docs.
